# Architecture Checklist: Student Self-Enrollment

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the architecture obligations for this slice, capped at five items
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK001 - Are the hexagonal obligations (domain rules independent of frameworks, use cases through ports, inbound adapters, outbound adapters) written so a reader can judge a design without relying on the directory tree alone? [Clarity, Constitution §IX, Plan §Project Structure]
  - Review 2026-10-14: accepted. Plan §Architectural obligations supplies implementation-independent criteria: dependency direction, business-rule ownership, port interaction, composition-root wiring, and responsibility-based review checks. Directory structure illustrates the split and is not the basis for compliance.
- [x] CHK002 - Is the "thin route" requirement specific about which decisions belong in the inbound adapter and which must remain in the use case? [Clarity, Constitution §X, Gap]
  - Review 2026-10-14: accepted. Plan §HTTP adapter and use case separates transport duties from business decisions. The adapter may parse and validate request structure, construct a command or query, invoke a use case, and map the application outcome to HTTP. It must not determine eligibility, entity existence, or business success or failure. User-facing wording must preserve any exact outcome text required by the specification.
- [x] CHK003 - Is "unnecessary coupling" between the student, course, programme, and inscription capabilities defined with explicit allowed and forbidden dependencies? [Ambiguity, Constitution §XI]
  - Review 2026-10-14: accepted. Plan §Cross-capability dependencies defines data ownership, identifier-only references, and port-based coordination. It prohibits cross-capability domain imports, shared value objects, repository access, and direct use-case calls. A database foreign key is a storage choice, not a domain dependency.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK004 - Are requirements defined for a conflicting enrollment, including a concurrent duplicate, so both the failure and the unchanged prior inscription are specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Research §Transaction and uniqueness]
  - Review 2026-10-14: satisfied. Spec §FR-007 and §FR-012 require a failed enrollment to leave the existing inscription and any stored grade unchanged. Research §Transaction and uniqueness requires rollback and the same already-enrolled outcome for a concurrent uniqueness conflict. No further behavioral requirement is needed. Follow-up: implementation tasks must include an integration test for that concurrent outcome.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK005 - Do the constitution rule that domain invariants are not a storage design and the plan's persistence-conflict decision state the same obligation for where the uniqueness rule lives? [Consistency, Constitution §X, Constitution §III, Research §Transaction and uniqueness]
  - Review 2026-10-14: satisfied. The business layer owns the uniqueness rule. The database supplies an atomic guarantee against concurrent duplicates. Rollback does not move that rule into persistence. The adapter exposes a persistence conflict, and the use case interprets it as already enrolled. Plan §Uniqueness conflict and Research §Transaction and uniqueness now state those three duties separately.
